test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 22 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about linear velocity?

options.text: Linear velocity is constant for uniform motion.
Linear velocity depends on displacement and time.
It is the rate of change of displacement.
The SI unit of linear velocity is {m/s}² .

solution:
The correct answer is __**The SI unit of linear velocity is m/s2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Linear velocity** is defined as the **rate of change of displacement** with respect to **time**. It indicates how fast an object is changing its position in a specific direction. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• The mathematical formula for **velocity** is **v = s / t**, where **s** represents **displacement** and **t** represents the **time interval**. This shows that the value of velocity is directly dependent on both the change in position and the duration of the motion. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• In **uniform motion**, an object covers **equal displacements** in **equal intervals of time** along a straight line. Because neither the magnitude (speed) nor the direction changes, the **linear velocity remains constant** throughout the motion. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• The **SI unit** of **linear velocity** is **meters per second (m/s)**. The unit **m/s2** (meters per second squared) is the **SI unit of acceleration**, which measures the rate at which velocity changes over time. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• Velocity is a **vector quantity**, meaning it is characterized by both **magnitude** and **direction**. A change in either the speed or the direction of an object will result in a change in its velocity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Difference between Speed and Velocity:** While **speed** is a **scalar quantity** that only accounts for how fast an object is moving, **velocity** is the **vector** counterpart that specifies the **direction of motion**. For example, **50 km/h** is speed, while **50 km/h towards the North** is velocity.
 
• **Average Velocity:** This is calculated as the **total displacement** divided by the **total time taken** for a journey. Unlike average speed, the average velocity can be **zero** if the starting and ending points are the same (zero displacement).
 
• **Instantaneous Velocity:** This refers to the velocity of an object at a **specific instant in time** or at a specific point in its path. It is often measured by the speedometer of a vehicle combined with a compass for direction.
 
• **Dimensional Formula:** In physics, the dimensional representation of **linear velocity** is **[M0 L1 T-1]**, where **M** is mass, **L** is length, and **T** is time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Acceleration:** It is the **rate of change of velocity**. If an object's velocity increases, decreases, or changes direction, the object is said to be **accelerating**. Its unit is **m/s2**.
 
• **Negative Velocity:** Velocity can be **negative**, **positive**, or **zero**, depending on the chosen coordinate system and the direction of the **displacement**.
 
• **Uniform Circular Motion:** Even if an object moves at a **constant speed** in a circle, its **linear velocity** is **not constant** because its **direction** is continuously changing at every point along the circular path.
 
• **Relative Velocity:** This is the velocity of an object with respect to another **observer** or reference frame. For instance, the velocity of a moving train appears different to a person standing on the platform compared to a person in another moving train.
